title: UP BOARD CLASS 3 — Environmental Studies | Biodiversity
description: Subject-wise test on Biodiversity (Environmental Studies) for UP BOARD CLASS 3. 25Q.
subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals lives in water?

options.explanation: Lions are land animals.
Elephants are land animals.
Fish live in water.
Monkeys are land animals.

questions.explanation: Fish are aquatic animals, meaning they live in water. Lions, elephants, and monkeys are land animals.
questions.hint: Think about where each animal typically lives.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a big and strong plant with a thick woody stem?

options.explanation: Grass is small and does not have a thick woody stem.
Shrubs are medium-sized with multiple woody stems but not as large as trees.
Trees have thick woody stems and are large.
Creepers grow along the ground and do not have thick woody stems.

questions.explanation: Trees are characterized by their large size, strong woody stems (trunks), and branches. Grass is small, a shrub is medium-sized with multiple woody stems, and a creeper grows along the ground.
questions.hint: Consider the size and structure of each plant type.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which animal gives us milk?

options.explanation: Tigers are wild animals and do not give milk.
Cows give milk.
Foxes are wild animals and do not give milk.
Bears are wild animals and do not give milk.

questions.explanation: Cows are domestic animals that are raised for their milk, which is a common food source for humans. Tigers, foxes, and bears are wild animals and do not provide milk for human consumption.
questions.hint: Think about animals commonly domesticated for milk production.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which part helps a bird to fly?

options.explanation: Legs are used for walking.
Beaks are used for eating.
Wings help birds fly.
The tail helps with steering and balance.

questions.explanation: Birds use their wings to generate lift and propulsion, allowing them to fly. Legs are for walking, beaks for eating, and the tail helps with steering and balance.
questions.hint: Consider the primary function of each bird part mentioned.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: A rabbit eats carrots. A fox hunts rabbits. What does the fox eat?

options.explanation: The fox hunts rabbits, not grass.
The fox hunts rabbits, not carrots.
The fox eats rabbits.
The fox hunts rabbits, not leaves.

questions.explanation: The question describes a simple food chain. The rabbit eats carrots, and the fox eats the rabbit. Therefore, the fox eats rabbits.
questions.hint: Follow the food chain described in the question.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: We get wood from which part of a tree?

options.explanation: Flowers are not used for wood.
Leaves are not used for wood.
The stem (trunk) of a tree is used for wood.
Roots are not typically used for wood.

questions.explanation: The woody part of a tree that is used for timber and other wood products is its stem, also known as the trunk. Flowers, leaves, and roots have different functions and are not typically used for wood.
questions.hint: Think about which part of the tree is used for making furniture and other wooden items.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Read the two statements. Statement 1: A lion is a wild animal. Statement 2: A lion lives in a jungle. Which option is correct?

options.explanation: Statement 2 is also true.
Statement 1 is also true.
Both statements are correct.
Both statements are true.

questions.explanation: Lions are indeed wild animals, and their natural habitat is the jungle or savanna. Therefore, both statements are correct.
questions.hint: Evaluate each statement separately and then together.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Rina saw an animal with a long trunk and big ears in the zoo. It was grey in color. Which animal did Rina see?

options.explanation: Giraffes have long necks, not trunks.
Elephants have long trunks, big ears, and are grey.
Zebras have stripes.
Bears do not have trunks.

questions.explanation: The description of a long trunk, big ears, and grey color is characteristic of an elephant. Giraffes have long necks, zebras have stripes, and bears do not have trunks.
questions.hint: Consider the unique features of each animal mentioned.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: If all the trees in a forest are cut down, what might happen to the animals living there?

options.explanation: Cutting down trees reduces food sources.

options.text: They will find new homes easily.
options.explanation: Finding new homes may be difficult.

options.text: They will lose their homes and food.
options.explanation: Animals lose habitat and food when trees are cut down.
Cutting down trees does not make animals stronger.

questions.explanation: Trees provide shelter, nesting sites, and food (leaves, fruits, nuts) for many forest animals. If trees are cut down, animals will lose both their habitat and their food sources, making it difficult for them to survive.
questions.hint: Think about the role of trees in the forest ecosystem.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Why is it important to have many different types of plants and animals in nature?

options.text: So that some animals can eat all other animals.
options.explanation: This would disrupt the balance of nature.

options.text: So that the world looks colorful.
options.explanation: While aesthetics are a benefit, it is not the primary reason.

options.text: So that nature stays balanced and healthy.
options.explanation: Biodiversity helps maintain a balanced and healthy ecosystem.

options.text: So that we can keep them as pets.
options.explanation: This is not the primary ecological benefit.

questions.explanation: Having a variety of plants and animals (biodiversity) is crucial for a balanced and healthy ecosystem. Different species play different roles in food chains, pollination, and nutrient cycling, all of which contribute to the overall health and stability of nature.
questions.hint: Consider the benefits of biodiversity in an ecosystem.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals gives us milk?

options.explanation: Tigers are wild animals and do not provide milk.
Cows are domestic animals that are commonly kept for their milk.
Elephants do not provide milk for human consumption.
Bears are wild animals and do not provide milk.

questions.explanation: Cows are domestic animals that are commonly kept for their milk.
questions.hint: This animal is often found on farms and is known for its white liquid product.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which part helps most birds to fly?

options.explanation: Legs help birds to walk or perch but do not aid in flying.
Birds use their wings to generate lift and propel themselves through the air, enabling them to fly.
A beak is used for eating and other functions but does not help in flying.
The tail helps in steering and balance but is not the primary organ for flying.

questions.explanation: Birds use their wings to generate lift and propel themselves through the air, enabling them to fly.
questions.hint: This part is attached to the sides of a bird's body.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a tree?

options.explanation: Rose plants are shrubs with thin stems and do not grow as tall as trees.
A mango plant grows tall with a thick, woody stem and branches, which are characteristics of a tree.
Mint is a herb with a soft stem and does not grow tall like a tree.
Money plant is a climber with a weak stem and requires support to grow.

questions.explanation: A mango plant grows tall with a thick, woody stem and branches, which are characteristics of a tree. Rose and mint are shrubs/herbs, and money plant is a climber.
questions.hint: This plant grows tall and has a strong, woody stem.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Where do lions usually live?

options.explanation: Lions do not live in ponds as they are land animals.
Nests are typically made by birds, not lions.
Lions are wild animals that typically live in dens, caves, or thickets within forests or grasslands.
Stables are places where domestic animals like horses are kept, not lions.

questions.explanation: Lions are wild animals that typically live in dens, caves, or thickets within forests or grasslands.
questions.hint: This is a natural shelter where lions rest and protect their young.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: I have a long trunk and big ears. I love to eat bananas and sugarcane. Who am I?

options.explanation: Giraffes have long necks but do not have trunks or big ears like elephants.
The description of a long trunk and big ears is a distinct characteristic of an elephant, and they are known to eat bananas and sugarcane.
Horses do not have trunks or big ears.
Monkeys do not have trunks or big ears.

questions.explanation: The description of a long trunk and big ears is a distinct characteristic of an elephant, and they are known to eat bananas and sugarcane.
questions.hint: This animal is the largest land mammal and is known for its trunk.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Some plants are weak and need support to grow upwards by wrapping around other objects. What are they called?

options.explanation: Trees have strong, woody stems and do not need support to grow.
Shrubs have multiple woody stems but do not typically need support to grow.
Creepers grow along the ground and do not wrap around objects to climb.
Climbers are plants with weak stems that cannot stand upright on their own and require support from other plants, walls, or structures to grow upwards.

questions.explanation: Climbers are plants with weak stems that cannot stand upright on their own and require support from other plants, walls, or structures to grow upwards.
questions.hint: These plants use other structures to climb and grow taller.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Why is it important to plant more trees?

options.explanation: Trees clean the air by absorbing pollutants and producing oxygen.

options.text: They give us shade and clean air.
options.explanation: Trees are crucial for our environment as they provide shade and produce oxygen, which helps to clean the air we breathe.
Trees do not make loud noises; they provide a peaceful environment.
Trees grow in various environments, not just deserts.

questions.explanation: Trees are crucial for our environment as they provide shade and produce oxygen, which helps to clean the air we breathe.
questions.hint: Trees help improve the environment by providing a natural resource.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which group contains only animals that live in water?

options.explanation: Lions, tigers, and bears are land animals.
Fish, whales, and octopuses are all aquatic animals, meaning they live exclusively in water.
Cows, goats, and sheep are domestic land animals.
Parrots, pigeons, and crows are birds that live on land.

questions.explanation: Fish, whales, and octopuses are all aquatic animals, meaning they live exclusively in water. The other options include land animals or birds.
questions.hint: These animals spend their entire lives in water.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Imagine a place that is very hot and dry, with lots of sand and very little water. Which animal is most likely to live comfortably there?

options.explanation: Polar bears live in cold, icy regions, not hot, dry deserts.
Camels are uniquely adapted to desert environments, with features that allow them to survive in hot, dry conditions with limited water.
Dolphins live in water and cannot survive in deserts.
Monkeys live in forests and cannot survive in hot, dry deserts.

questions.explanation: Camels are uniquely adapted to desert environments, with features that allow them to survive in hot, dry conditions with limited water. Polar bears live in cold regions, dolphins in water, and monkeys in forests.
questions.hint: This animal is known as the 'ship of the desert' and can survive without water for long periods.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: A big forest has many different types of trees, animals, and birds. If many trees in this forest are cut down, what is the most likely consequence for the animals?

options.explanation: Cutting down trees reduces food sources for animals.
Trees provide shelter (homes, nests) and food for many forest animals. Cutting down a large number of trees directly destroys their natural habitat and food sources.

options.text: They will learn to fly higher.
options.explanation: Animals cannot suddenly learn to fly higher; their natural habitats are destroyed.
Cutting down trees may affect the local climate but is not the most direct consequence for the animals.

questions.explanation: Trees provide shelter (homes, nests) and food for many forest animals. Cutting down a large number of trees directly destroys their natural habitat and food sources, forcing them to find new homes or face danger.
questions.hint: Animals depend on trees for their survival.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which of these plants has a thick, woody stem and lives for many years?

options.explanation: Herbs have soft, non-woody stems and typically live for a short period.
Shrubs have woody stems but are usually smaller than trees and do not live as long.
Trees have thick, woody stems and can live for many years.
Creepers have weak stems that trail on the ground and do not live long.

questions.explanation: Trees are characterized by their thick, woody stems (trunks) and their ability to live for many years, unlike herbs, shrubs, or creepers.
questions.hint: Look for plants with strong, hard stems that stand tall and live long.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Which animal lays eggs and has feathers on its body?

options.explanation: Dogs are mammals and do not lay eggs or have feathers.
Fish lay eggs but do not have feathers.
Birds lay eggs and have feathers on their bodies.
Cows are mammals and do not lay eggs or have feathers.

questions.explanation: Birds are the animals that lay eggs and have feathers covering their bodies, which are distinct features not found in dogs, fish, or cows.
questions.hint: Think of animals that can fly and have feathers.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: A goat eats grass and leaves. What kind of animal is a goat?

options.explanation: Carnivores eat only meat, not plants.
Goats eat only plants like grass and leaves, making them herbivores.
Omnivores eat both plants and meat.
Scavengers eat dead animals.

questions.explanation: Animals that eat only plants, like grass and leaves, are called herbivores. Carnivores eat only meat, omnivores eat both plants and meat, and scavengers eat dead animals.
questions.hint: Consider what the goat eats to determine its diet type.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: In a forest, we can see lions, deer, monkeys, and various birds. Why is it good to have so many different types of animals in a forest?

options.text: They all eat the same food.
options.explanation: If they all ate the same food, competition would be high, and the ecosystem would suffer.

options.text: They help each other live and keep the forest healthy.
options.explanation: Different animals contribute to the ecosystem in various ways, maintaining balance and health.

options.text: Only one type of animal is enough.
options.explanation: A single type of animal cannot fulfill all ecological roles, leading to imbalance.

options.text: They all sleep in the same place.
options.explanation: Sleeping habits do not contribute to the health of the forest ecosystem.

questions.explanation: Different types of animals play different roles in an ecosystem (like eating different foods, spreading seeds, or controlling populations), which helps to keep the forest balanced and healthy. If only one type of animal existed, the ecosystem would become unbalanced.
questions.hint: Think about how diversity in animals helps maintain balance in nature.
questions.subject: upbo3-evs

questions.question: Imagine a world where there are only dogs and no other animals or plants. What problem would this cause for the dogs?

options.explanation: Having many friends does not address the issue of food scarcity.

options.text: Dogs would not have enough different kinds of food to eat.
options.explanation: Dogs need a variety of food sources, including plants and other animals, to survive.
Dogs cannot learn to fly, and this does not solve the food problem.
The size of dogs is not related to the availability of food sources.

questions.explanation: Dogs are omnivores, meaning they eat both plants and other animals. If there were no other animals or plants, dogs would quickly run out of food and would not be able to survive, highlighting the importance of biodiversity for food sources.
questions.hint: Consider the dietary needs of dogs and the role of other plants and animals in their survival.
